_readme: Andhra Pradesh citizen contact and grievance directory. Every entry was read off a government page and carries that page. Research pass 30 Aug 2026. Nothing here is transcribed from an aggregator, a directory site or a news report — a wrong helpline number is worse than a missing one.
_warning: Most district collectorate phone numbers, most department phone numbers and emails, and every district's pre-2022 parent district are NOT in this file because no government page I could reach publishes them; they are null, and 'unavailable' says exactly which page a person in Andhra Pradesh should open to get them.

grievance_systems.name: PGRS / Mee Kosam - Andhra Pradesh Public Grievance Redressal System
grievance_systems.what_for: The state's current one-stop public grievance platform. Described on the portal as 'a universal grievance redressal helpline that allows citizens to directly raise their issue to the Chief Minister's Office'. Use it to (a) register an individual or household-level grievance, (b) follow up on a registered grievance, (c) enquire about government services and schemes.
grievance_systems.how_to_file: Online at https://pgrs.ap.gov.in or https://meekosam.ap.gov.in (authentication is by OTP to the Aadhaar-linked mobile number, with UIDAI verification and consent); by the mobile app; or in person at the Collectorate grievance session held on Mondays.
grievance_systems.what_happens_next: The grievance is routed to the responsible officer and can be tracked with the registration number.
grievance_systems.time_limit: Not stated on the pages I could read.

grievance_systems.name: Spandana
grievance_systems.what_for: Andhra Pradesh's public grievance platform as described on district collectorate sites - 'a public problem solving platform' for citizen petitions to any state, district or zonal official.
grievance_systems.how_to_file: Submit through the Spandana citizen portal, or hand the application to any state/district/zonal level official; you get a receipt with an application number, and the application is scanned and forwarded to the responsible officer.
grievance_systems.what_happens_next: Quoting the East Godavari collectorate page: 'Each issue is timed with a specific time limit for resolution'; if it is not resolved within the deadline the case 'will be sent to the higher level officer for resolution immediately'. Track status by calling 1100 or 1800-425-4440 with the application number.
grievance_systems.time_limit: A per-issue time limit exists but the specific limits are not published on the page; the same page states typical current resolution runs 3-6 months.
grievance_systems.notes: spandana.ap.gov.in exists (it is returned as an official result) but could not be fetched from this environment. District pages published in 2025-26 point citizens to PGRS/Mee Kosam, so PGRS appears to be the live front door; Spandana branding is still used on several district pages. Verify which is current before publishing.
grievance_systems.contact: Director ESD (Meeseva), Vijayawada - +91-7032642837, mobile +91-7032642836, helpmeekosam-ap@nic.in (as published on eastgodavari.ap.gov.in)

grievance_systems.name: Grama/Ward Sachivalayam citizen services portal (AP Seva)
grievance_systems.what_for: The single window for applying for state services at the village or ward secretariat - certificates, welfare scheme applications, land and civil-supplies services. This is the first rung of almost every escalation ladder below.
grievance_systems.how_to_file: Walk in to your Grama Sachivalayam (village) or Ward Sachivalayam (urban) with the required documents and get an acknowledgement with an application number, or apply online. The former URL https://vswsonline.ap.gov.in now redirects (HTTP 302) to https://apseva.ap.gov.in.
grievance_systems.what_happens_next: The application is routed to the Digital Assistant / concerned functionary; status is tracked by application number.
grievance_systems.time_limit: Service-wise limits are the ones notified under the AP Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2017 (see 'law_or_go' in the escalations). Not published on a page I could read.
grievance_systems.source_url: https://igod.gov.in/sg/AP/SPMA/organizations ; observed 302 redirect from https://vswsonline.ap.gov.in/#/home to https://apseva.ap.gov.in/

grievance_systems.how_to_file: At a MeeSeva centre, or online through the citizen portal at https://onlineap.meeseva.gov.in/CitizenPortal/UserInterface/Citizen/Home.aspx
grievance_systems.what_happens_next: An application number is issued and the service is delivered to the counter or online.

grievance_systems.name: CPGRAMS - Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (Government of India)
grievance_systems.what_for: Grievances against central government ministries, departments and organisations, and against state governments where the state is onboarded. Available 24x7.
grievance_systems.how_to_file: Online at pgportal.gov.in, through the CPGRAMS mobile app (Android/iOS), through UMANG, or at a Common Service Centre (CSC). Grievances sent by email are not entertained - filing on the portal is mandatory.
grievance_systems.what_happens_next: The grievance is routed to the public authority. After closure you can rate the disposal; if you rate it 'Poor' the system enables an appeal, which is tracked with the original grievance registration number.
grievance_systems.time_limit: The portal states you may seek help 'within a reasonable period of time' if there is no satisfactory resolution; no specific number of days is given on the page.

grievance_systems.name: Andhra Pradesh Information Commission (RTI second appeal and complaint)

grievance_systems.how_to_file: Not verified - the Commission's site could not be fetched from this environment.
grievance_systems.time_limit: Not verified from a government page (the RTI Act's own limits are 30 days for the PIO, 30 days for the first appeal, and 90 days to file the second appeal, but I did not read that from a page I could fetch).
grievance_systems.notes: URL confirmed by the Government of India's IGOD directory only. The site itself was unreachable; see 'unavailable'.

grievance_systems.how_to_file: Use Form I / Form II (available in English and Telugu) from the Downloads section of the site, together with the 'How to complain' guide.
grievance_systems.what_happens_next: Not stated on the page beyond the existence of an Investigation Wing; annual reports (2024-2025) are published on the site.

grievance_systems.name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP)
grievance_systems.what_for: Reporting cybercrime, including financial fraud, cyber-stalking and crimes against women and children. Run by the Ministry of Home Affairs. Also carries a 'Suspect Repository' where a citizen can check mobile numbers, emails and URLs linked to cybercriminals.
grievance_systems.how_to_file: Call 1930 immediately for financial fraud (so the transaction trail can be frozen), then register on the portal via 'Register a Complaint' and select 'FINANCIAL FRAUD' for money-loss cases.
grievance_systems.what_happens_next: The complaint is routed to the concerned state/UT law enforcement agency for action.
grievance_systems.time_limit: No time window is stated on the portal page.

grievance_systems.name: National Consumer Helpline (NCH 2.0), Department of Consumer Affairs
grievance_systems.what_for: Pre-litigation consumer grievance against a business - refunds, defective goods, deficient services.
grievance_systems.how_to_file: Call 1915 (8AM to 8PM, 17 languages), or use the portal, the NCH app, UMANG, WhatsApp +918800001915, or SMS. Documents can be uploaded to the complaint.
grievance_systems.what_happens_next: The complaint is taken up with the company; the citizen tracks it on the portal ('Track Your Grievance') and there is a callback facility. If it is not resolved, the next step is a formal complaint to a Consumer Commission.

grievance_systems.name: Andhra Pradesh State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (SCDRC)
grievance_systems.what_for: Statutory consumer adjudication in Andhra Pradesh - appeals from District Consumer Commissions and original complaints above the district pecuniary limit.
grievance_systems.how_to_file: Not verified - the Commission's site could not be fetched from this environment. Online filing for consumer complaints nationally is through the NCDRC's e-Daakhil portal.

escalations.law_or_go: The Andhra Pradesh Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2017 (Act No. 6 of 2018). Verified from the Government of India's India Code repository. Its scheme: s.5 - the Government notifies, by notification, which public services are covered and the 'stipulated time limit' for each; s.2(i) defines 'stipulated time limit' as 'the maximum time to provide the service by the public authority'; s.6 - 'The Public Authority shall designate Officer/Officers for providing Public Services under this Act' (the Designated Officer); s.9 - 'Every Designated Officer who fails to deliver the public service to a person within the stipulated time shall be liable to pay compensation to the applicant at such rates as may be prescribed'; s.10 and s.11 provide for an appeal to an Appellate Authority and revision by the Government. IMPORTANT: the Act itself fixes no days for any service - the actual number of days for each service comes from the Government notification under s.5, which I could not locate on a government page. Source: https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/9072/1/apps_delivery_guarantee_act%2c_2017.pdf (act page: https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/9072)
escalations.notes: Portals: Mee Bhoomi (https://meebhoomi.ap.gov.in) is described by the Government of India's IGOD directory as the 'Public Portal of Land Records' for AP; BhuNaksha (https://bhunaksha.ap.gov.in) is the cadastral map portal. I could NOT verify from any government page I could reach: (a) whether 'Webland' is still live and at what URL, (b) the status of the AP Land Titling Authority Act framework, or (c) any notified number of days for mutation. A title dispute (as opposed to a record error) is a civil matter for the civil court - the revenue ladder above can correct records but cannot decide title.

escalations.problem: Police - how to file an FIR, and what to do if a police station refuses to register one

steps.office: The police station with jurisdiction - give the information orally or in writing. Dial 100 (or 112) to bring police to you; AP Police also send officers to the complainant in cases involving women and children rather than requiring a station visit.
steps.what_to_bring: A written complaint signed by you (AP Police state: 'In case of registration of a case, a written complaint along with the signature is necessary as per law'). Carry ID and any evidence; ask for and keep the FIR number and a free copy of the FIR.
steps.time_limit: An FIR must be registered without preliminary inquiry where the information discloses a cognizable offence.

steps.office: If the offence happened outside that station's jurisdiction - insist on a ZERO FIR. The station must register it, write 'Zero FIR' in the FIR number column and forward it to the station with jurisdiction through the Superintendent of Police.
steps.what_to_bring: Same as above; note the officer's name and the date/time you attended.
steps.time_limit: Immediate - no preliminary inquiry is permitted.

steps.office: REFUSAL - REMEDY 1: send the substance of the information in writing, by post, to the District Superintendent of Police (in a city commissionerate, the Commissioner of Police / DCP). Under BNSS s.173(4) the District Superintendent of Police may order investigation of a cognizable offence, and on such an order the station house officer must register the FIR.
steps.what_to_bring: A written complaint plus proof that you approached the station (dated acknowledgement, registered-post receipt, or the date and officer's name).
steps.time_limit: Not stated in the source.
steps.portal: Also lodge it in parallel on https://pgrs.ap.gov.in and, for a cyber offence, https://cybercrime.gov.in

steps.office: REFUSAL - REMEDY 2: apply to the jurisdictional Judicial Magistrate. Under BNSS s.175(3) a court may order investigation of a cognizable offence, and on that direction the officer must register an FIR. No preliminary inquiry is permitted and investigation must proceed without delay.
steps.what_to_bring: Your written complaint, the proof of refusal, and an affidavit; the application is made to the Magistrate having jurisdiction.
steps.time_limit: Not stated in the source.

steps.office: Parallel routes: State Human Rights Commission / NHRC (14433) for police misconduct; Anti-Corruption Bureau on 14400 if a bribe was demanded; the Superintendent of Police's weekly grievance day.
steps.what_to_bring: Everything above.
steps.time_limit: Not published on a page I could read.

escalations.law_or_go: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 46 of 2023) - s.173 (information in cognizable cases, including s.173(4): order of the District Superintendent of Police) and s.175(3) (a court may order investigation). Verified from a state police department circular published on a gov.in domain: https://megpolice.gov.in/sites/default/files/circular-no.3-2024-first-information-report.pdf . The BNSS text itself is at https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/20099/1/A202346.pdf but the relevant sections were beyond the portion of that PDF I could read.
escalations.notes: IMPORTANT SOURCING CAVEAT: the BNSS s.173(4)/175(4)-(3) remedy above is verified from a MEGHALAYA Police circular, not an Andhra Pradesh page - BNSS is central law and applies identically in AP, but no AP police page I could reach states the refusal remedy. The AP Police citizen portal (https://citizen.appolice.gov.in) was unreachable from this environment, so AP's own e-FIR / online complaint route is unverified.

unavailable.what_a_human_should_do: Check your district's /helpline/ page, https://eraktkosh.mohfw.gov.in for blood banks, the AP Forest Department at https://forests.ap.gov.in for wildlife rescue, and the Labour department at https://employment.ap.gov.in. Do not publish any of these numbers until you have seen them on a government page.

unavailable.what: Andhra Pradesh Transport Department (RTA - driving licences, vehicle registration). It is not in IGOD's AP department list. Its site appears to be aptransport.org, which is NOT on a .gov.in domain, so it is excluded here under the sourcing rules.
unavailable.what_a_human_should_do: Check whether a district collectorate site links it - e.g. https://tirupati.ap.gov.in/district-transport-department/ or https://spsnellore.ap.gov.in/transport-department/ - and use the district page as the corroborating government source before publishing the domain.

unavailable.what: An Energy Department, Home Department, Housing Department, Environment Department, Minority Welfare Department, Skill Development Department and Infrastructure & Investment Department entry with its own secretariat website. IGOD does not list these as AP departments; only their corporations, commissions and utilities are listed, and those are what appear in 'departments' here.
unavailable.what_a_human_should_do: Open the department directory on https://www.ap.gov.in and add each secretariat department's own site. Cross-check against https://goir.ap.gov.in, which files every G.O. by issuing department and therefore lists the true secretariat department names.

unavailable.what: Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and Vidyut Ombudsman procedure and time limits for Andhra Pradesh. https://vidyutombudsman.ap.gov.in returned no readable body content and https://aperc.gov.in rendered only a notifications list.
unavailable.what_a_human_should_do: Open https://vidyutombudsman.ap.gov.in for the Ombudsman's address and the appeal form, and https://aperc.gov.in for the APERC (CGRF and Ombudsman) regulations, which contain the statutory time limits.

unavailable.what_a_human_should_do: Open https://scdrc.ap.nic.in/pdf/ContactUs.pdf directly - it is the Commission's own published contact PDF.

unavailable.what: Conflicting helpline values seen across AP government pages: Tirupati's site lists the Citizen's Call Center as 155300 while Guntur and Visakhapatnam list Citizen Services as 1902; Tirupati lists 'Women Helpline: 1091' while Visakhapatnam lists 'Women Helpline: 181' and india.gov.in lists 1091 as the Anti-Obscene Calls Cell; Sri Sathya Sai's helpline page lists 'Fire: 100', which contradicts the national fire number 101.
unavailable.what_a_human_should_do: Dial-test 1902, 155300 and 1091 before publishing any of them, and publish 101 (not 100) for fire. The Sri Sathya Sai page's 'Fire: 100' is a mistake on that page and is not reproduced as a fire number in this file.
